summary: Right-handed baseball pitcher at the balance point: standing on the right leg on the rubber, left knee lifted above hip height, hands together at the chest, body turned away from the plate.

environment.name: rubber
environment.text: Pitcher's plate (rubber) 61 x 15 cm, white, on top of a mound 25 cm above home plate; the front edge of the plate is 18.44 m from the rear point of home plate.

rules.why: lead knee flexed about 108 deg at maximum height
lead hip flexed about 112 deg, thigh above horizontal
lead knee about 65 % of height above the rubber
hands together (ball in the glove) at chest height

text.action: a right-handed baseball pitcher at the balance point of the windup
text.core: Standing tall on the right leg on the rubber, right knee slightly bent; left knee lifted above the hip, lower leg hanging, toes relaxed; body turned side-on and slightly past, left shoulder pointing toward home plate; ball hidden in the glove, both hands together at chest height; head level, chin over the glove shoulder.
text.gaze: Eyes on the catcher's mitt over the left shoulder.
cues: balance over the pivot leg at the top of the leg lift
controlled coil, trunk not leaning back
kinetic: stillness before the drive, dust on the rubber
jersey hanging still, cap brim shading the eyes
stadium lights rim-lighting the lifted knee

sources.cite: Driveline OpenBiomechanics, baseball_pitching (100 pitchers, 411 fastballs, 1.85 +/- 0.07 m): means computed from the dataset's point-of-interest and full-signal files (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; only summary numbers used here)
A Clinician's Guide to Analysis of the Pitching Motion (2019): balance point, 90/90 arm position, MER about 170 deg
Windup vs stretch, Am J Sports Med 2024 (higher knee lift from the windup)
